card.statement:
[9] [10, Theorem 7.2]

Let ${\zeta_{\imath}}\in X_{\imath}$ and $(b_{1},b_{2})\in B_{\mathbb{I}_{\bullet}}\times B$ .

(1)

There is a unique element $u=b_{1}\diamondsuit^{\imath}_{\zeta_{\imath}}b_{2}\in\dot{\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ such that

$u(\eta^{\bullet}_{\lambda}\otimes\eta_{\mu})=(b_{1}\diamondsuit_{\zeta_{\imath}}b_{2})_{w_{\bullet}\lambda,\mu}^{\imath}\in L^{\imath}(\lambda,\mu),\text{ for all }\lambda,\mu\gg 0\text{ with }\overline{w_{\bullet}\lambda+\mu}={\zeta_{\imath}}.$

(2)

The element $b_{1}\diamondsuit^{\imath}_{\zeta_{\imath}}b_{2}$ is $\psi_{\imath}$ -invariant.

(3)

The set $\dot{\textbf{B}}^{\imath}=\{b_{1}\diamondsuit^{\imath}_{\zeta_{\imath}}b_{2}\mid{\zeta_{\imath}}\in X_{\imath},(b_{1},b_{2})\in B_{\mathbb{I}_{\bullet}}\times B\}$
forms a $\mathbb{Q}(v)$ -basis of $\dot{\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ .
card.label: Theorem 3.2

paper.title: Quantum symmetric pairs
paper.abstract: This is a survey of some recent progress on quantum symmetric pairs and applications. The topics include quasi K-matrices, $\imath$Schur duality, canonical bases, super Kazhdan-Lusztig theory, $\imath$Hall algebras, current presentations for affine $\imath$quantum groups, and braid group actions.
